title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 nears flagship scores by spending far more tokens
friendlyTitle: Claude Sonnet 5.5 gets strong scores but uses many more tokens
summary: Artificial Analysis places Claude Sonnet 5.5 at number two on its Intelligence Index at maximum effort, two points behind Opus 5.5, with particularly strong terminal and knowledge-work results. That setting also used about 193,000 output tokens per index task—the highest the evaluator has measured—and cost roughly 50% more per task than Sonnet 5 despite unchanged per-token pricing.
friendlySummary: Independent tests put Sonnet 5.5 close to the leading model at its highest effort setting. It reached that result by producing more tokens, which raised the cost of each task.
whyItMatters: Per-token prices and headline benchmark scores can conceal the real cost of a completed job. Buyers should compare quality, latency and total tokens at the effort setting they will actually use, then reserve expensive maximum-effort runs for tasks that justify them.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A low price per token does not always mean a cheap result. Measure the full cost and time of your real tasks at the settings you plan to use.
